body.statement: Can the contact-set multiplier handle be developed into a confidence set that retains uniform \((1-\alpha)\) coverage over \(\mathcal M_\eta\), has asymptotically exact rather than conservative coverage whenever the limiting contact-set Gaussian maximum has a continuous quantile, is first-order no wider than \(\mathcal C_n\) at every law with unique separated lower and upper simplex branches, and is strictly narrower on a nonempty observable region where inactive scores from \(\widetilde f_\beta^-\) and \(\widetilde f_\beta^+\) enlarge the all-branch Gaussian quantile?
body.justification: The all-branch envelope buys robustness by paying a potentially avoidable width cost away from ties.
body.gap: Fang and Santos (2019) motivates estimated contact derivatives, but uniform adaptation across this two-endpoint rational frontier with singular scores is not settled by the cited results.
body.consumer: A successful construction would deliver shorter sensitivity intervals on a certified regular region without sacrificing protection near branch switches.

obligation.what_is_open: A complete contact-set directional-multiplier construction satisfying uniform coverage, pointwise exactness at every continuous limiting contact quantile, first-order domination of the all-branch interval, and strict improvement on a certified nonempty observable region.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen contact-set definition is only a handle.  Screening inclusion and unique-branch reduction follow from the finite rational atlas, but uniform calibration along root-\(n\) local approaches to multiway faces requires a directional critical-value theorem that remains valid with singular and vanishing scores.  Strict narrowing at the fixed \(1-\alpha\) quantile additionally requires a strict stochastic-quantile comparison, which is not implied merely by deleting an inactive score.
obligation.attempted: Screened branches at tolerance \(\kappa_n/\sqrt n\) with \(\kappa_n\to\infty\) and \(\kappa_n/\sqrt n\to0\); used uniform Lipschitz control to retain all locally reachable active branches and compared the screened multiplier maximum pointwise with the all-branch maximum.  This proves the inclusion and unique-separated-branch parts but does not close the joint uniform directional-quantile and strictness assertions.
obligation.partial_result:
Let \(\kappa_n\to\infty\) with \(\kappa_n/\sqrt n\to0\), and screen by
\[
 \widehat{\mathcal A}_s=
 \left\{\beta:\left|\widetilde f_\beta^s(\widehat z)-
 \widetilde F_s(\widehat z)\right|\leq\kappa_n/\sqrt n\right\}.
\]
Uniform Lipschitz bounds and root-\(n\) tightness imply that every branch active at the true law, and every branch reachable along the segment from \(z\) to \(\widehat z\), belongs to \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_s\) with probability tending to one uniformly.  A multiplier maximum over these screened scores is pointwise no larger than the all-branch maximum; at a law with a unique branch separated by a positive value gap, the screen selects that branch with probability tending to one.  What remains unproved is a single calibrated directional critical value that simultaneously (i) preserves this inclusion uniformly along all \(n^{-1/2}\)-local approaches to multiway faces with singular scores, (ii) has exact limiting coverage at every continuous contact-set quantile, and (iii) has a rigorously certified strict quantile reduction on a nonempty observable region at the fixed level \(1-\alpha\).
